1:1.t: The writer of Hebrews is not named. Early Christians suggested Paul, Barnabas, Apollos and others; the KJV's heading attributes it to Paul.

1:6.t: A quotation of Deuteronomy 32:43 from the Greek (compare Psalm 97:7).

1:8.t: "Your throne, O God": the psalm addresses the king as God; Hebrews applies it to the Son.

2:6.t: A quotation of Psalm 8:4-6 from the Greek. "And set them over the works of Your hands": the KJV's reading; some early manuscripts do not have these words.

3:6.t: "Firm to the end": the KJV's reading; some early manuscripts do not have these words.

4:2.t: "Because it was not combined with faith in those who heard it": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "because they did not share the faith of those who obeyed".

4:8.t: "Joshua": the KJV's "Jesus", the Greek form of the name Joshua. See Acts 7:45.

5:6.t: A quotation of Psalm 110:4. "Melchizedek": the KJV's "Melchisedec". See Genesis 14:18-20.

5:7.t: "Because of His reverent submission": the KJV's "in that he feared"; Greek eulabeia, godly fear, reverence.

7:1.t: See Genesis 14:17-20. Salem is probably Jerusalem (Psalm 76:2).

7:17.t: Quotations of Psalm 110:4. "In the order of Melchizedek" in verse 21: the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words there.

7:21.t: Quotations of Psalm 110:4. "In the order of Melchizedek" in verse 21: the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words there.

8:8.t: A quotation of Jeremiah 31:31-34, the longest Old Testament quotation in the New Testament.

8:12.t: "And their iniquities": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words.

9:2.t: "The Holy Place": the KJV's "the sanctuary". See Exodus 25-26.

9:4.t: "Golden censer": the KJV's reading; the Greek thymiaterion can also mean "altar of incense", which stood just outside the inner curtain (Exodus 30:1-6).

9:5.t: "Atonement cover": the KJV's "mercyseat"; Greek hilasterion, the lid of the ark where the high priest sprinkled blood on the Day of Atonement. See Romans 3:25.

9:7.t: See Leviticus 16, the Day of Atonement.

9:11.t: "Good things to come": the KJV's reading; some early manuscripts read "good things that have come".

9:26.t: "At the culmination of the ages": the KJV's "in the end of the world".

10:5.t: A quotation of Psalm 40:6-8 from the Greek. The Hebrew of Psalm 40:6 reads "my ears You have opened"; the Greek reads "a body You prepared for Me".

10:23.t: "Faith": the KJV's reading; the Greek elpis means "hope".

10:34.t: "In my chains": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "with those in prison".

10:37.t: A quotation of Isaiah 26:20 and Habakkuk 2:3-4 from the Greek.

11:5.t: A quotation of Genesis 5:24 from the Greek.

11:21.t: See Genesis 47:31 in the Greek, which reads "staff" where the Hebrew reads "bed".

11:35.t: These verses recall the Maccabean martyrs and Jewish traditions about the prophets; tradition says Isaiah was sawn in two. "They were tempted": the KJV's reading; some early manuscripts do not have these words.

12:5.t: A quotation of Proverbs 3:11-12 from the Greek.

1:2.t: "The worlds" (Greek tous aionas): the KJV's reading; literally "the ages", the universe in time and space.

1:3.t: "Radiance" (Greek apaugasma): the KJV's "brightness", the shining out of light from its source. "Exact representation" (Greek charakter): the KJV's "express image", the stamp made by a seal on wax. "Being" (Greek hypostasis): the KJV's "person", God's essential nature.

2:10.t: "Pioneer" (Greek archegos): the KJV's "captain"; archegos means leader, founder, pioneer, the one who goes first and opens the way. See Acts 3:15. "Perfect" (Greek teleiosai): to bring to completion, to qualify fully for His role, not to correct a flaw. A key word in Hebrews (5:9, 7:28).

2:17.t: "Make atonement" (Greek hilaskesthai): the KJV's "make reconciliation". In the Greek Old Testament hilasterion is the "mercy seat", the lid of the ark where the high priest sprinkled blood on the Day of Atonement. The word carries both the turning away of God's wrath (propitiation) and the cleansing of sin (expiation). See Romans 3:25.

4:9.t: "A Sabbath rest" (Greek sabbatismos): a word apparently coined by the writer. God's rest, pictured by the Sabbath and the land of Canaan, is still offered to those who believe.

4:12.t: "Alive and active" (Greek zon ... energes): the KJV's "quick, and powerful".

4:15.t: "Tempted in every way ... yet He did not sin": Jesus' temptations were real, and so He can sympathize; His sinlessness is why He can save.

5:8.t: "Learned obedience ... made perfect": "perfect" (Greek teleioo) means to bring to completion, to qualify fully, not to correct a flaw (see 2:10). The eternal Son, as a man, learned by experience what obedience costs, and was fully qualified to be Savior.

6:4.t: One of the most debated passages in Hebrews. Christians understand it as describing true believers who could lose their salvation, people who experienced much but never truly believed, or a hypothetical warning meant to keep believers faithful. The writer immediately adds that he is "convinced of better things" for his readers (6:9).

6:19.t: "Anchor" (Greek ankyra): an early Christian symbol of hope. "Behind the curtain": the Most Holy Place, where God's presence dwelt.

6:20.t: "Forerunner" (Greek prodromos): one who runs ahead to prepare the way for others to follow.

7:3.t: "Without father or mother, without genealogy": Genesis records no parents or death for Melchizedek. The writer reads this silence as a picture of the Son's eternal priesthood.

7:22.t: "Guarantor" (Greek engyos): the KJV's "surety", one who stands security for a debt or promise.

7:25.t: "Completely" (Greek eis to panteles): the KJV's "to the uttermost", fully, and for all time.

7:27.t: "Once for all" (Greek ephapax): a key word in Hebrews (9:12, 10:10). Christ's sacrifice never needs repeating.

8:6.t: "Covenant" (Greek diatheke): the KJV's "covenant" here, "testament" elsewhere. Diatheke can mean a will or testament, but here it translates the Hebrew berit, covenant. See Matthew 26:28.

9:15.t: "Covenant ... will" (Greek diatheke): the same word means both. The writer plays on the double meaning: a will takes effect only at the death of the one who made it, and Christ's covenant is sealed by His death.

9:22.t: "Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness": the principle behind the whole sacrificial system (Leviticus 17:11), fulfilled in Christ.

10:10.t: "Made holy ... made perfect": the believer's standing before God is complete through Christ's one sacrifice, while the life of holiness continues ("are being made holy").

10:14.t: "Made holy ... made perfect": the believer's standing before God is complete through Christ's one sacrifice, while the life of holiness continues ("are being made holy").

10:26.t: "Deliberately keep on sinning": in context, a settled rejection of Christ after knowing the truth (10:29), not ordinary failure. Compare 6:4-6.

11:1.t: "Confidence ... assurance" (Greek hypostasis ... elenchos): the KJV's "substance ... evidence". Hypostasis can mean the underlying reality or the confident assurance; elenchos means proof or conviction. Faith treats God's promises as real and certain.

11:17.t: "His only son" (Greek monogenes): the KJV's "only begotten", meaning the one and only, unique son. See John 1:14. Abraham had another son, Ishmael, but Isaac was the unique son of the promise.

11:26.t: "Disgrace for the sake of Christ": the KJV's "the reproach of Christ". Moses shared in the reproach that God's anointed people, and ultimately the Messiah, would bear.

12:1.t: "Witnesses" (Greek martys): those listed in chapter 11, who testify by their lives to faith, like spectators in a stadium.

12:2.t: "Pioneer and perfecter" (Greek archegos ... teleiotes): the KJV's "author and finisher". archegos means leader, founder, pioneer, the one who goes first and opens the way; the teleiotes brings it to completion. See 2:10.

12:17.t: "No place for repentance" (Greek metanoias topon): Esau could not change his father's decision, or could not undo his act, though he sought the blessing with tears.

13:8.t: "The same yesterday and today and forever": compare 1:12. Christ's unchanging nature is the ground for steady faith.
